IDENTITY ORIENTED PROGRAMMING · 77 SAMPLES · 30 LESSONS

Data in $shapes, messages in @events, tags in #marks, templates in &builders.

VeinScript is a language where the building block of a program isn't an object or a function. It's an identity. You declare the data an identity can carry, called shapes and written with a dollar sign. You declare the tags it can wear, called marks and written with a hash. And you declare the messages it can send, called events and written with an at sign. All behaviour lives in shards, and a shard never calls anything. It targets every identity that matches and acts on each one. When two shards write the same field in the same tick, the field itself says how the writes combine, for example 'folds sum', so the order the shards run in never matters. The same model runs a game loop, a chat across three console windows, and a website assembled from fragments. It comes with one compiler, an interpreter and a C# backend, plus a desktop IDE that lets you step through time and watch your identities change one tick at a time.

30 lessons~118 min in full~29 min core path ★code cut live from samples/

The mental model

Everything is an identity. Behaviour never calls behaviour. A program makes identities with spawn() and hangs data and tags on them. Behaviour then finds them with a query.

  • Shape $Health: the fields an identity carries (a component), e.g. attach $Health to e { hp: 5 }.
  • Mark #Enemy: a tag with no fields, e.g. mark e #Enemy / unmark. $Enemy and #Enemy are two different things.
  • Event @Damaged: a message with a payload. emit queues it and hear @Damaged as d { … } reacts to it. Every event carries provenance (d.from.name, d.cause).
  • Shard: the only place behaviour lives. It is a set of blocks: run once, each tick, settled, every N, hear @E. Inside a block, target $Health #Enemy as self { … } visits every identity that carries all of those.
  • SF / fn: an SF is a named sequence of emits and never returns. An fn computes a value and returns it.
  • Builder + bring: a template. The name of its output field decides what it makes: markup→@Html, css→@Style, code→@Script, line→@Print, and no output field→@BuilderName. A mark member makes it an identity template, so bring Unit(10, 6) does spawn + attach + mark. $Shape includes copy a shape's fields into the parameter list, and arguments bind by position.
  • Bundle: the module, written bundle Game by you { … }. Everything in it is private by default. Only shared("…") members of a publicator can be used from another bundle, either as *Author.Bundle.Publicator.member or as a bare name after need "Author.Bundle". An app manifest loads bundles. The first one is the principal, and its start @E is the only boot event. The others join the same runtime.

Time: tick → commit → settled.

  1. run once seeds the world.
  2. Every each tick block runs. A write to a field is a contribution, and the shape says how contributions merge. With hp: int folds sum, two shards that each do hp -= 1 give hp - 2, whatever order they ran in.
  3. spawn happens immediately. attach/unattach/mark/unmark/destroy wait for the commit point, so no shard ever sees a half-changed world.
  4. settled runs after the folds are reconciled. That is where you read final values, such as death checks.

Events drain one at a time. Each event's structural changes are committed before the next event runs, so the next event sees what the last one built. Inside the event that made a change, the change is not visible yet.

Two execution models, one identity model. The reactive loop covers emit/hear/ShardView → @Response, console and network. The ECS tick loop covers target/each tick/settled/folds and is driven by --ticks N. Both run in the interpreter. The identity half also compiles to C# with veinc emit.

run once seeds the world→each tick: shards target and write→folds merge the writes→commit: mark / attach / destroy land→settled reads final values

Four sigils, four colours

The Workbench paints each sigil its own colour, and so does every code block on this page. On screen, the colour tells you what kind of name you're looking at before you read it.

$Health
Shape

Data an identity carries, as fields (a component). attach $Health to e { hp: 5 }

#Enemy
Mark

A tag with no fields. mark e #Enemy, unmark e #Enemy

@Damaged
Event

A message with a payload. emit queues it and hear @Damaged as d { … } reacts

&Heading
Builder

A template, referenced by name, e.g. *Vein.Web.Elements.&Heading(…). A local one is used as bring Unit(10, 6)

First video: identities and time

1

Two shards, one hp ★

Read a complete VeinScript program: shapes carry data, marks tag identities, shards target every match, and folds sum merges writes made in the same tick.

~6 min · entities.vein

Open withTwo pieces of code, neither knows the other exists, and both subtract one from the same number in the same frame. In most languages one write wins or you reach for a lock. Here the number drops by exactly two, every time, whichever runs first.

Say
  • shape $Health declares data an identity can carry, and hp: int folds sum says what happens when several shards write hp in one tick: their deltas are added.
  • run once seeds the world. Inside repeat 3, spawn() makes a new identity, attach $Health to e { hp: 5 } gives it data, and mark e #Enemy tags it. $ means shape, # means mark.
  • Drain and Poison are two separate shards with the same line: target $Health #Enemy as self { self.Health.hp -= 1 }. Neither calls the other, and neither knows the other exists.
  • target is the loop over identities: it visits every identity carrying both $Health and #Enemy, and self.Health.hp reads that identity's field.
  • The Undertaker reads hp in settled, which runs after the tick's writes are reconciled, so the value it sees is final. At zero or below it does mark self #Dead and unmark self #Enemy. Entity is the id of the identity the loop is on.
  • Run it for three ticks: every enemy prints hp 3, then 1, then -1, then 'died'. That is 5 minus 2 per tick, so both writes landed.
  • Live: delete folds sum and run again. Now hp falls by only one per tick, so a write was silently lost, and veinc exec on the edited file flags a Drain x Poison conflict on $Health.hp. Put folds sum back.

Data, a seeded world, and two shards writing the same field

Reading the result after the tick settles

Run it
Watch out
  • Use veinc run … --ticks 3 on camera. The header's veinc render line prints an emit trace instead of the hp lines.
  • Removing folds sum still passes veinc check. Only the run and veinc exec show the lost write, so rehearse the edit on a copy.
  • Read a folds field in settled. A mid-tick read is not reconciled yet (RULES 13).
  • #Enemy and #Dead are never declared, so their names go unchecked and a typo would silently create a new mark (RULES 16).
  • With no spawn() the world is empty and every target matches nothing (RULES 10).
  • The lines print through emit *Vein.Console.Io.@Print. Don't explain it yet: l04 reveals that printing is an event.

Three lines of spawn, attach and mark per enemy is a lot of ceremony for 'make an enemy', and a builder turns it into one.

2

bring: one line per identity ★

Declare an identity template with builder … { $Shape mark #Mark } and create identities with bring, including bring N.

~3 min · entities_template.vein

Open withLast lesson took three lines to make one enemy: spawn, attach, mark. A builder does it in one line. bring Mob(12) lowers to exactly those three statements, and bring Unit(12, 6) to four, with one attach per shape.

Say
  • builder Unit { $Health $Shield mark #Unit } has no body. The shapes and the mark it lists are its whole definition.
  • The mark member makes it an identity template: bring Unit(12, 6) means spawn, attach $Health with hp 12, attach $Shield with sp 6, and mark #Unit.
  • Arguments bind by position across the includes in declaration order: $Health takes hp, then $Shield takes sp. Mob and Ward include one shape each, so they take one argument.
  • bring 2 Unit(4, 2) makes two separate identities, e4 and e5, not one shared one.
  • Wear targets $Health $Shield #Unit, and several shapes in one query is an AND. After tick one e1 reads hp=11 sp=4, while e2 (a Mob) and e3 (a Ward) never change, because neither carries both shapes.
  • Live: veinc scaffold samples/entities_template.vein Unit prints a ready-to-paste bring Unit( call with one slot per field, each labelled with its type and the shape it came from.

Two shapes, three one-line templates, and a shard that uses them

Run it
Watch out
  • Without a mark member, or a mark carried by an included shape (RULES 15c), a $Shape include only copies fields. bring Mob(12) then emits @Mob, attaches nothing, and target $Health never sees it. veinc check warns VS0237 when nothing hears that event (RULES 8).
  • Ask veinc scaffold for the argument order instead of counting (RULES 9). Keep the header's scaffold listing off screen: it shows ? slots, while the real command prints base, // hp: int from $Health REQUIRED — give it a value.
  • bring 2 Unit(…) as n is VS0222, because a count cannot be combined with as (RULES 7b).
  • A builder's output field decides what it makes, and a mark member makes an identity (RULES 5, 7).

Now the timing question from lesson one: when exactly does a mark, an unmark or a destroy take effect?

3

Nothing changes mid-frame ★

Predict when structural changes land: spawn is immediate, while attach, unattach, mark, unmark and destroy wait for the commit point, and settled sees the result.

~4 min · entities_destroy.vein

Open withThree shards remove things this frame, and a fourth, running in the same frame, counts what's left. It sees nothing removed, and that is the guarantee, not a bug.

Say
  • mark #Alive and mark #Guarded on their own lines, outside any shard, declare the two marks. Lesson 1 never declared #Enemy. Declaring any mark makes the compiler check mark names in this bundle, and lesson 11 comes back to that. builder Mob { $Health, $Shield mark #Alive mark #Guarded }: each of the three bring Mob(…) calls gives an identity both shapes and both marks, with hp 10, 20 and 30.
  • Three removal verbs of three sizes: Cull does unmark m #Alive under 15 hp, Disarm does unattach $Shield from m, and Reap does destroy m over 25 hp.
  • During counts in each tick, the same phase as the removals, using var alive = 0 counters. var declares a local you reassign (alive = alive + 1), while lesson 1's let e = spawn() names a value you don't mean to change (the compiler does not enforce that today). After runs the identical counts in settled.
  • Frame 1 prints during alive 3 shielded 3 entities 3, then after alive 1 shielded 0 entities 2. Every removal was queued and landed together at the commit point.
  • The 10-hp mob still exists, it just isn't #Alive. The 30-hp one is gone completely. That's why entities is 2 and alive is 1.
  • Live: cut shard During, paste it above Cull, and run again. The numbers don't change: no shard ever sees a half-changed world, so shard order can't matter.
  • Live in the Workbench: open the file, go to the Runtime panel, press Boot, then Step ▸ once, and watch the entity browser go from three identities to two.

Three mobs, each with two shapes and two marks

unmark, unattach, destroy: one shard each

The same count, during the tick and after it

Run it
Watch out
  • attach, unattach, mark, unmark and destroy are DEFERRED to the commit point. destroy m does not make m vanish mid-frame (RULES 11).
  • A structural change is invisible inside the phase or event that made it, so seed worlds in run once and read in a later phase (RULES 12, 12b).
  • A mark-only query such as target #Alive as a is VS0236. Name a shape too, as target $Health #Alive as a does.
  • Frames 2 and 3 both print 'alive 1 shielded 0 entities 2', because nothing is left to remove.
  • There is no != or !: write not (a == b) and not x (RULES 2).

Everything so far has run on a clock. Most programs react to something instead, like a typed line or a request, and every line we've printed was already an event.

First video: events, failure and apps

4

Printing was an event all along ★

Write a reactive program: name and declare a boot event, hear events with an as binding, and emit events with payloads.

~3 min · console.vein

Open withEvery line we've printed so far was an emit. Nothing in VeinScript calls the terminal. The terminal is just another listener.

Say
  • bundle App { … } wraps the whole program. A bundle is VeinScript's module (lessons 1-3 had one too, just off-screen), and with no by in its header (compare bundle Store by you {) its author is local. Inside it, start @Boot { } names the entry event, event @Boot { } declares it, and veinc run fires it once.
  • Shard Main is only two hear blocks, with no run once and no each tick. Unlike the clock-driven shards so far, it does nothing until an event arrives.
  • emit *Vein.Console.Io.@Print { text: … } writes a line, and hear *Vein.Console.Io.@Input as i fires once for each line you type. Nothing writes to stdout or reads stdin directly: even the print helper you'll see in lesson 5 is an SF that just emits @Print.
  • Read the path left to right: * starts it, Vein is the author, Console the bundle, Io the publicator, and @Print the event.
  • as i binds the payload, so i.text is the typed line, and + joins strings.
  • Live: run it, type hello and get you said hello, type one more line, then end with Ctrl+Z and Enter on Windows (Ctrl+D on Unix).

A whole interactive program: one entry event, one shard, two handlers

Run it
Watch out
  • A newline ends a statement. If you wrap "you said " + i.text, the + must END the first line (RULES 1).
  • A string literal stays on one line (RULES 3).
  • start @Boot { } alone is enough today: delete event @Boot { } and veinc check still says ok and the run looks the same. Keep the declaration anyway, because it is what makes @Boot show up in veinc events samples/console.vein, which lists no events without it.
  • Piping empty input ends the run right after the prompt, because the run stops at stdin EOF. Type live in a real terminal.
  • The old use Console form is retired (VS0338). Stdlib names are reached by * path or with need "Author.Bundle" (RULES 18).

Shards can't call each other, so where does reusable logic go? Into two kinds of function, split by what they produce.

5

fn computes, SF emits ★

Choose between fn (returns a value) and SF (a named sequence of emits), and call shared ones from another bundle by qualified path.

~3 min · functions.vein

Open withVeinScript has functions, two kinds of them, and the split is not about syntax. It's about what they produce: a value, or events.

Say
  • fn bonus(streak: int) -> int computes and returns, so it can go anywhere a value can. Parameters are written name: Type.
  • SF announce(label: string, value: int) has no return type, and its body is an emit. An SF is a named emit sequence, and a call to it stands alone as a statement.
  • fib is a local fn that recurses. It needs no shared to be called inside this bundle.
  • shared("…") inside a publicator is the only thing that crosses a bundle boundary, and the string is a label shown in completion.
  • Scoreboard calls announce("fib(10)", fib(10)), an fn result passed into an SF call, and the output reads fib(10): 55 after streak 3 bonus: 15 and streak 99 bonus: 50.
  • Across bundles: *Vein.Math.Scalars.clamp(99.0, 0.0, 10.0) is Vein.Math's shared fn and prints clamp(99, 0, 10) = 10, and *Vein.Console.Io.print(…) is Vein.Console's shared SF, which emits @Print for you.

A shared fn, a shared SF, and a local recursive fn

Four kinds of call: local and cross-bundle, fn and SF

Run it
Watch out
  • -> T on an SF is VS0105, and return outside an fn is VS0107 (SYNTAX-DECISIONS D6).
  • Only shared("…") inside a publicator crosses a bundle boundary (RULES 17). A label over 160 characters warns VS0243 (RULES 17d).
  • An SF's emits queue. They do not print at the moment of the call (RULES 21).
  • Whole floats print without .0, so clamp shows 10, not 10.0.

An SF names a sequence of emits. Put many emitters together and you get a web page that no function returns: shards each emit a fragment.

6

A website assembled from events ★

Serve a site with several routes and a form, where shards contribute @Html fragments per route and a ShardView assembles the response.

~4 min · web_site.vein

Open withNo handler in this site returns a page. Shards emit fragments, one view listens, and the page is whatever arrived.

Say
  • need "Vein.Web" makes the stdlib builders Heading, Paragraph and Link usable by bare name. None of them has a mark member. Each has a markup = … output field instead, and a builder's output field name decides what it makes. So bring Heading("Say hello") spawns no identity and writes no markup: it queues an @Html fragment. A css field would make @Style, code @Script and line @Print.
  • Routing is a plain if r.path == "/greet". Every page shard hears every @Request and only contributes when its path matches.
  • Same path, two methods. On GET, Greet brings a heading, emits the form as a raw @Html string and links home. On POST it reads the submitted field as r.who, an ordinary payload field.
  • Router emits @Render and is declared after the page shards, so @Render queues behind every fragment. ShardView Page appends each h.markup to var html and answers @Response when @Render arrives.
  • if not (html == ""): no fragments means no response, and the server turns that into a 404. There is no != in the language.
  • Live: veinc serve samples/web_site.vein --port 8080, open http://localhost:8080/, click 'say hello', submit Ada and get 'Hello Ada', then try /nope for the 404.

One need brings in the web vocabulary

One route, two methods: the form and its answer

@Render queues last; the view assembles or stays silent

Run it
Watch out
  • Don't read out the comment at lines 63-64. It's stale: Vein.Web's @Request has no ?, and form and query values simply arrive as extra payload fields.
  • The form is one string literal, and a literal cannot span lines (RULES 3). A + at the start of the next line would begin a new statement (RULES 1). To wrap it, end the line with +, which also works inside the emit payload.
  • bring and emit queue. A view answering @Request directly would see an empty page, which is why Router exists and must stay below the page shards (RULES 21).
  • veinc serve gives every request a fresh interpreter, so nothing persists between visits (RULES 22).
  • Offline fallback: veinc render samples/web_site.vein /greet --set method=POST --set who=Ada prints Hello Ada. Under Git Bash, set MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 for / arguments (RULES 23).

Something will go wrong in a program like this, such as a bad row or a divide by zero, and there's no try/catch to reach for.

7

No try/catch: failure is a message ★

Collect every diagnostic in a program with one hear, raise your own with info/warn/error, and see a runtime fault stop only its own block.

~3 min · diagnostics.vein

Open withI'm going to divide by zero on purpose, and the program keeps going.

Say
  • Collector is the catch: hear *Vein.Diagnostics.Report.@DiagnosticRaised as d. d.severity is an int (0 info, 1 warning, 2 error), and Collector prints each with its own prefix: note, WARN, ERROR.
  • A catch belongs to the code that failed, but a hear belongs to whoever cares. Collector gets every diagnostic in the program, and no failing shard knows it exists.
  • Validate brings a row with an empty title and rank -1, then calls *Vein.Diagnostics.Report.info, warn and error. Nothing failed here: the program made a judgement and reported it.
  • Compute evaluates 5 % 0, a remainder by zero, and the runtime raises the same event: ERROR | Compute (once): Attempted to divide by zero. It names the shard and the phase.
  • The block stops, not just the statement: 'THIS LINE NEVER PRINTS' never prints. Carry_on still runs in settled and prints '-- the program is still alive --' and both rows.
  • The collected lines appear after the plain prints because Collector answers with another @Print, which joins the back of the same queue.

The catch: one hear for every diagnostic in the program

Diagnostics you raise yourself

A real fault stops its block; the rest of the program carries on

Run it
Watch out
  • Don't repeat the header's 'the same six lines still appear'. This run prints four diagnostic lines: three raised and one fault.
  • Carry_on is in settled because the rows brought in Validate's run once commit at the end of that phase. Another run once block would see nothing (RULES 12b).
  • emit queues, so the Collector's lines arrive one hop after an inline @Print (RULES 21).
  • Validate reports but does not reject. Both rows still exist and are printed.
  • A file or network failure is a message too: @FileMissing, @Failed, @Undelivered (RULES 28b).

Collector heard an event from Vein.Diagnostics, a bundle it never wired up by hand. The same mechanism lets a whole program be several bundles sharing one queue.

8

An app is a list of capabilities ★

Link several bundles into one runtime with an app manifest, where only the principal boots and the others react across bundles.

~3 min · app_capabilities

Open withDelete one line of this manifest and the app stops invoicing, without touching a single other file.

Say
  • app Shop loads three bundles. The first load is the principal, and Store's start @Ordered { item: "widget", qty: 3 } is the app's single boot event.
  • Store shares @Ordered and @Shipped from publicator Orders. Inside its own bundle it just writes @Shipped.
  • Billing declares no start. It hears *you.Store.Orders.@Shipped (author, bundle, publicator, event) and emits its own shared @Invoiced.
  • The manifest comment says Audit, the third load, watches both of the others. All three bundles share one event queue.
  • Run it: the banner reads principal 'Store' boots; 3 bundle(s) linked into one runtime, then Store, Audit, Billing and Audit print in queue order.
  • Live: comment out load "Billing.vein" and run again. Invoicing disappears, Audit still sees the order, and no other file changed.

The whole app: three loads, the first one boots

The principal: shared events and the one start

A capability: no start, it only reacts

Run it
Watch out
  • Declare a cross-bundle event with shared("…") inside a publicator. That's the bundle's API (RULES 17). Only veinc symbols checks it, with VS0305 on an unshared *you.Store.Orders.@Shipped. veinc check and veinc run don't, and Billing still hears an unshared @Shipped.
  • An event's identity is Author.Bundle.Name, so other bundles write *you.Store.Orders.@Shipped (RULES 20).
  • Read the output as a queue, not a call stack: '[Audit] saw order' prints before '[Billing] invoicing' (RULES 21).
  • Only the principal's start fires. A start in any other loaded bundle does not (VS0331). Older LANGUAGE.md text says every bundle boots, which is wrong.

That's the whole model in one sitting. The deep dives start with everyday code: four loops, and no for.

Deep dive: everyday code

9

Four loops, and no for

Pick the right loop (while, repeat N as i, target <list> as x, target $Shape #Mark as e) and use break and continue in all four.

~4 min · loops.vein

Open withThere's no for and no in in VeinScript. There are four loops instead, and each one says what it's walking.

Say
  • while i < 10 with continue at 2 and break at 5 prints 1, 3, 4.
  • repeat 3 as r counts from 0, and r is the same number the built-in Index gives: 'repeat r=0 Index=0'.
  • A count is a limit, not a promise: break at r == 2 stops repeat 10 after 'capped r=0' and 'capped r=1'.
  • words("alpha beta skip gamma") returns a list and target … as w walks it. continue skips "skip", so three words are numbered.
  • The fourth loop is the identity loop in Report: target $Score #Player as p with the same continue. Make brings Ada 30, Grace 20 and Alan 10, and Alan's 10 points never print.
  • Report runs in each tick, not in Make's run once, because a bring commits at the phase boundary. With --ticks 2 the two score lines print twice.

while, repeat, and a loop over a list

The identity loop, with the same continue

Run it
Watch out
  • for, in and loop are refused on purpose (SYNTAX-DECISIONS D3).
  • There is no !=: inequality is not (a == b) (RULES 2).
  • A target in the same run once as the brings would find nothing (RULES 11, 12b).
  • The comment above Report says 'This is the second tick'. It means the phase after run once, and Report prints on tick 1 too.
  • Index is the nearest loop's 0-based counter (RULES 14c).

Loops walk data. The next thing most programs need is a state that changes over time, and a clean way to branch on it.

10

A state machine with enum and match

Declare an enum inside the shape that owns it, advance it by comparing cases, and read it back with match … when … else.

~3 min · enum_state.vein

Open withAn enum in VeinScript lives inside the data it describes. There's no top-level enum at all.

Say
  • enum State { Kickoff, Play, Over } is declared inside shape $Match, and state: State types the field.
  • bring Referee(State.Kickoff, 0): a case is a value you can pass around, bound by position (state, then clock).
  • Each tick, Whistle bumps the clock, moves Kickoff to Play, and moves Play to Over once m.Match.clock >= 3. Logic is written in words, like and.
  • Commentary reads the state back in settled with match m.Match.state { when Kickoff … when Play … when Over … else … }.
  • The output is t1 in play, t2 in play, t3 full time, t4 full time. 'awaiting kickoff' never prints because Whistle moved on in frame 1 before settled ran, and 'NO STATE' never prints either. That absence is the check.

An enum inside its shape, advanced each tick, read back with match

Run it
Watch out
  • A top-level enum is VS0102 by design (SYNTAX-DECISIONS D11).
  • SAMPLES.md §3 still lists enum as lexed but unimplemented, and match_orders.vein's header says an enum case can't be a value. This file runs and is in check-backend, so don't repeat either claim.
  • when only exists inside match. There is no when cond { } conditional (SYNTAX-DECISIONS D2).
  • A misspelt case in a value, like State.Kikoff, is VS0242 at the spelling. A misspelt when arm is not checked: when Paly compiles clean and never matches, so t1 and t2 print NO STATE. The else arm is what catches it.
  • A match arm may start its own line, unlike } else { after an if (RULES 2b).

match branches on a value. Marks are the other way to sort identities into kinds, and they stay on an identity across ticks.

Deep dive: identities and templates

11

$Enemy and #Enemy: marks are tags that stay

Declare marks, combine several in a query, swap them at runtime, and know that declaring marks turns on name checking.

~4 min · entities_marks.vein

Open withThis file gives a shape and a mark the exact same name, on purpose.

Say
  • mark #Enemy, mark #Awake and mark #Spent at the top declare the marks. Declaring any mark switches on name checking for this bundle.
  • shape $Enemy { hp: int folds sum } is data, and #Enemy is a tag. Same word, different sigil, two different things: Seed attaches one and marks the other.
  • Drain targets $Enemy #Enemy #Awake, so it needs the shape and both marks. Several marks in one query are an AND.
  • Reaper, in settled, marks #Spent and unmarks #Awake and #Enemy once hp hits 0, so that enemy leaves Drain's query.
  • Ledger matches only #Spent. Run five ticks: tick three prints each 'spent' line, and from tick four on only 'ledger: eN is spent' lines appear. The tag stayed on the identity.
  • Live: misspell #Enemy as #Enmey in Drain's target and veinc check warns VS0218, because the mark isn't declared.

Declared marks, a same-named shape, a two-mark query

Every query so far came back in spawn order. Next, reading the same identities in an order you choose, and numbering them as you go.

14

target … by and Index: order and position

Sort a query at read time with by Shape.field (ascending, stable, ordinal), and number, cut off and stripe rows with Index.

~4 min · entities_ordered.vein · entities_index.vein

Open withFive rows, brought in scrambled order. The same rows print in three different orders in one frame, and not one id moves.

Say
  • Seed brings delta 4, alpha 1, Zeta -2, charlie 3, bravo 1, and a plain target $Row #Row yields exactly that spawn order.
  • target $Row #Row by Row.rank as r sorts when the rows are read, so -2 Zeta comes first. Ints sort numerically, and by comes before as.
  • by Row.title compares strings ordinally, so capital 'Zeta' comes before every lowercase name. The sort is stable: alpha and bravo both have rank 1 and keep spawn order.
  • Entity says which identity, and Index says which iteration, starting at 0. In entities_index.vein, (Index + 1) + ". " numbers six rows from 1 with no counter variable.
  • if Index < 3 is a top-three cutoff, Index % 2 == 0 stripes (0 alpha, 2 gamma, 4 epsilon), and Index == 0 finds the first row.
  • Index counts position in the order the loop already yields. It never sorts. If you run veinc run samples/entities_index.vein --ticks 1 after the main run, crop it after 'first is alpha': its last section prints three rows under '-- first two of the wide ones --' (see Watch out).

Five rows, deliberately out of order

Spawn order, by rank, by title, and ties

Index: numbering, a cutoff, striping, the first row

Run it
Watch out
  • Ascending only, by one field. There is no descending order (SYNTAX-DECISIONS D13).
  • Strings compare ordinally, so capitals come first. by takes a Shape.field, not an expression, so there is no by lower(Row.title). For a case-insensitive order, give the shape a field holding lower(title) and sort by Row.thatField. In a plain comparison, lower(a) < lower(b) and lower(a) == lower(b) already ignore case (RULES 14b, 28, 28e).
  • entities_index.vein's last block is stale: its label says 'first two of the wide ones' but it prints three rows, because the if Index < 2 filter was removed. Keep it off screen, or relabel or restore it before filming.
  • count is lexed but unimplemented, so there is no built-in row count. To find the last row, count first (var n = 0, then target $Row #Row as r { n = n + 1 }) and test Index == n - 1 in a second loop. The header comment calling the last row 'not expressible' is out of date (RULES 14c).
  • Index belongs to the nearest loop only (RULES 14c).

Five ways to call the same builder

?: leave a required field empty on purpose

Watch out

18

Two forces, one velocity

Use stdlib shapes through qualified builder includes, watch a constant per-tick force build up into acceleration, and see the step lag one frame behind.

~4 min · motion.vein

Open withGravity and wind don't know about each other. Every frame both push the same velocity, one on y and one on x, and the object falls faster and faster along a straight slant.

Say
  • Mover includes *Vein.Transform.Spatial.$Position and *Vein.Transform.Spatial.$Velocity: bring Mover(0.0, 100.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0) gives position first, then velocity.
  • Ticker carries Vein.Time's $Clock, and bring Ticker(0.0, 0.5) sets now to 0 and delta to 0.5.
  • Gravity does m.Velocity.y -= 4.9 and Wind does m.Velocity.x += 1.0. The stdlib declares every axis of $Velocity with folds sum, which is what lets two forces on the same axis both land. Here they push different axes, so each write would land even without folds.
  • Velocity keeps its value from tick to tick, so adding the same force every tick makes it grow, and a constant force becomes acceleration: v goes '1, -4.9', then '2, -9.8', then '3, -14.7'.
  • Step moves by velocity * 0.5, yet frame 1 prints 'at 0, 100'. Step reads the velocity as it stood at the end of the previous frame, which is an explicit Euler step.
  • The standard library ships shapes, not behaviour, so integrating position is the app's own Step shard. Live: step it in the Workbench Runtime panel and watch Position and Velocity change tick by tick.

Deep dive: pages from events

20

A page by hand: fragments, a Kernel and a view

Build the request → fragments → ShardView → response pipeline by hand, and see that declaration order is queue order.

~3 min · site.vein

Open withNo function returns this web page. Two shards shout pieces of it, and a view stitches them together. Move one shard and the page goes blank.

Say
  • publicator SiteApi declares the four events itself: @Request, @Html, @Render and @Response, each with a shared("…") label.
  • Header and Body both hear @Request as req and each emits its own @Html { markup: … } fragment. Nobody calls them.
  • Kernel also hears @Request and emits @Render. It's declared after the content shards, so its event queues behind their fragments.
  • ShardView Page keeps var html: string, appends every fragment with html += f.markup, and emits @Response with status 200 when @Render arrives.
  • veinc render samples/site.vein / fires one request with no socket. The trace shows Header, Body, Kernel, then Page, followed by HTTP 200 and the page, and it names the event @local.Site.Html.
  • Live: move shard Kernel above Header and render again. You get HTTP 200 with <html><body></body></html>, because @Render was queued first.

Content shards, a Kernel, and the ShardView that assembles them

Run it
Watch out
  • Under Git Bash set MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 for a / argument, or it becomes C:/Program Files/Git/ (RULES 23). site.vein never reads the path, so it still renders, but a routed site such as web_site.vein then prints '(no @Response emitted for C:/Program Files/Git/)'.
  • emit queues, and the queue drains only after every handler of the current event finishes. That's why Kernel's position matters (RULES 21).
  • An event's full name carries its bundle (RULES 20). Don't repeat the older 'events unify by bare name' wording from LANGUAGE-TOUR or STDLIB.md.
  • The · trace lines go to stderr, while the status and body go to stdout.
  • Don't use mypage.vein, shaped.vein or handles.vein for this idea: they currently render empty pages.

25

HTTP as a request and a reply

Call an HTTP service with @Fetch, and handle @Fetched and @Failed separately.

~3 min · net_fetch.vein

Open withA web request with no await, no callback and no promise: one event goes out, one event comes back. And a 404 is not a failure here.

Say
  • Boot emits *Vein.Net.Http.@Fetch { url, method, body } for httpbin's /ip once, and Poller emits another for /uuid every 5 seconds.
  • Results hears @Fetched and prints r.status + " " + r.url, then the body.
  • A 404 or 500 still arrives as @Fetched, because the server answered. @Failed means no answer at all (bad host, refused connection, timeout) and carries f.reason.
  • The request runs off the event loop and posts its result back, so every 5 keeps firing while a slow host hangs.
  • Live: run it, watch the IP reply and then a fresh UUID every 5 seconds, and end with Ctrl+Z and Enter.

Fetch once, poll on a timer, handle the reply and the silence

Run it
Watch out
  • The first reply is your public IP address from httpbin.org/ip: blur or crop that line in the edit.
  • It needs internet access to httpbin.org. Offline, every request arrives as @Failed.
  • @Fetch also has a headers field that this sample leaves out. A missing field reads as empty and is not warned about (RULES 26).
  • var n in Poller is incremented but never read.
  • To use a JSON body, parse it with fromJson(r.body) (RULES 24b).

HTTP asks a stranger. Peers are two Vein programs that know each other and prove who they are.

26

Peers: @Listen, @Link and a signed audience

Connect two programs over TCP with a shared key, and filter whose messages are heard.

~4 min · net_peer.vein · net_spoke.vein

Open withThe hub is never told where the spoke lives, and it still answers every ping.

Say
  • The hub emits *Vein.Net.Peer.@Listen { as: #Hub, at: 9700, key: "shared-secret" }: as is who this program is on the network.
  • The spoke listens as #Spoke on 9701, then @Link { name: #Hub, at: "127.0.0.1:9700", … }. Linking registers a route and connects nothing.
  • Pinger sends @Send { to: #Hub, text: "ping " + round } every 2 seconds, the same shape as a console send.
  • Frames are signed with the key, so the hub's hear … audience #Spoke is a real barrier, not a request. Inbox, with no audience, still sees every message.
  • Trusted replies with @Send { to: m.from, … } to a peer it never linked. It learned the route from the signed frame.
  • Live: start the spoke first, and each ping comes back as @Undelivered. Then start the hub in a second terminal, and the spoke prints 'Hub replied: ack ping N'. A mark used as a value is its bare name, so there is no #.

The hub: listen, a trusted handler, an inbox

The spoke: listen, link, ping

Run it
Watch out
  • net_peer's header says its @Send is 'byte for byte' the console version. The shape is the same, but the path is *Vein.Net.Peer.@Send, not *Vein.Console.Io.@Send.
  • @Listen refuses an empty key, and a wrong key looks like silence, because authentication happens at the receiver.
  • Ports 9700 and 9701 collide with the chat sample, so don't run them together.
  • Frames are encrypted under one static key. It isn't TLS: there is no forward secrecy and no certificate identity.
  • audience takes a bare mark (RULES 17b).

Put a roster of peers behind the hub and you have a chat server.

27

A networked chat in two files

Run a TCP chat where the server keeps its roster as entities and relays each line to everyone except the sender.

~6 min · chat

Open withLaptop on the left, laptop on the right, one server, and not one line of socket code. The server doesn't know a single address in advance.

Say
  • The server emits *Vein.Net.Peer.@Listen { as: #Server, at: 9700, key: "chat-secret" } once and never links a client.
  • The roster is made of entities: a newcomer becomes spawn() plus attach $Client with addr: m.from, and target $Client is how the server looks through it. var known: bool carries the answer out of the loop.
  • The relay skips the sender with if not (self.Client.addr == m.from), because there is no !=.
  • On the client, let first = not joined snapshots the state. The first line you type is your name, and @Listen { as: i.text, at: 0, … } makes it your network identity, with the OS picking the port.
  • @Link { name: #Server, at: ServerAddress(), … } registers the route, sending "is here" puts you on the roster, and audience #Server on Incoming admits only the server's frames.
  • Live: start the server (it prints 'server listening on 9700'), then a client in each of two more terminals or machines. Type bob in one and alice in the other, then hi bob.
  • The server prints '* bob joined' and 'alice: hi bob'. Bob sees alice's lines, and alice never gets her own line back.

The server: listen, keep a roster of entities, relay

The client: your first line is your identity

Only the server may be heard

Run it
Watch out
  • client.vein's ServerAddress() returns the placeholder "999.999.999.999:9700". Change it to "127.0.0.1:9700" (or the server machine's IP) before filming, or the client only reports that it can't reach the server.
  • The server machine must accept inbound TCP on 9700, and Windows may ask to allow it through the firewall the first time.
  • Every side must use the same key "chat-secret". A mismatched key shows up as silence, not as an error.
  • Several client.vein comments are stale (the address being typed in, alice.vein and bob.vein), so don't read them out.
  • attach is deferred (RULES 11), so the relay loop doesn't see the newcomer in the same handler. That's harmless, because the newcomer is the sender.

Every line in the chat was a string. The last part turns structured data and whole files into identities.

Deep dive: data and files

28

JSON in, identities, JSON out

Parse JSON with fromJson, bring one identity per record in sorted order with ordered by, and serialise a shape back with toJson.

~4 min · json_roundtrip.vein

Open withA string arrives, becomes a world you can query, and each record goes back out as JSON with its types intact.

Say
  • fromJson(payload) turns the string into plain data: objects become dictionaries and arrays become lists, so doc.rows is ordinary field access and len(doc.rows) prints 3.
  • The payload is four one-line string literals joined by +: each of the first three lines ends with a trailing +, which keeps the expression open (RULES 1, 3).
  • target doc.rows as row: $Row is an ascription: it declares what the outside data looks like, and fields are read directly as row.title. Today the compiler checks only that $Row exists (VS0233). A misspelt field such as row.titel still compiles and reads as empty.
  • ordered by rank { … } sorts the brings themselves. The payload arrived as 4, 1, -2, but the rows are spawned -2, 1, 4, so the plain query without by prints them in rank order.
  • toJson(r.Row) serialises the $Row shape on the identity in declaration order, for example {"title":"Zeta","rank":-2,"done":false}. Ints stay ints and bools stay bools.

A JSON string becomes plain data

One bring per record, sorted as they are brought

A plain query in rank order, and back out as JSON

Run it
Watch out
  • toJson takes a shape (r.Row), never the entity, because nothing can ask an entity which shapes it carries (RULES 14, 24b).
  • Ascribed rows read row.title, while a component query reads r.Row.title (RULES 27).
  • This is interpreter-only: veinc emit still prints the C# (to stdout, or into a folder with -o), but it also prints a note for each of fromJson() and toJson() saying it has no C# emission, so this file will not compile (RULES 24b).
  • Malformed JSON parses to null, not a crash (RULES 24b).
  • ordered by reorders only bring, and every key is evaluated first (RULES 14d, 14e). The report is in settled, so run with --ticks 1 or more.

JSON arrived as a string literal. Real data arrives from files, and a file is an event too.

29

Files are events: route them by tag

Write and read files through events, tag each request, and route every reply through one checked match f.tag.

~5 min · file_tags.vein

Open withFive files, one handler, and not one path spelled twice.

Say
  • There's no open, close or handle: @WriteFile answers @FileWritten, @ReadFile answers @FileLoaded, and either one answers @FileMissing when it fails.
  • Seed writes five files, and each write carries a tag: #Config, #Log, and a computed "slot" + (i + 1) for three saves.
  • Ask hears every @FileWritten and reads the file back with tag: w.tag. The runtime hands the tag back untouched.
  • Route's match f.tag has when #Config and when #Log arms. A mark in value position evaluates to its own name, and when is checked against the declared marks.
  • Computed tags can't be named in a when, so the slots land in else: bring Slot(slots, trim(f.text)) as s, then mark s #Save.
  • The third slot emits @SavesLoaded, a new event, so the Report shard that hears it sees all three #Save identities. The output ends 'save 1: level=3' to 'save 3: level=9'.
  • @FileMissing carries the tag too, so its handler routes with its own match m.tag and the same when #Config / when #Log arms. The failure path needs no path comparisons either.

Five writes, each tagged, three with computed tags

Read it back with the same tag

Success and failure, each routed by what the read was for

Run it
Watch out
  • Running it writes files under samples/out/ (gitignored). Paths resolve against the source file's folder, not the working directory.
  • The comment at line 42 says an undeclared mark is VS0210, and the header (line 30) and RULES 28c call a misspelled tag a compile error. The real diagnostic is VS0218, and it is a warning: a when #Confg typo prints 'warning VS0218: Mark #Confg is not declared in this bundle. known: #Config #Log #Save #Slot' and '0 error(s), 1 warning(s)', and veinc run still runs, printing 'untagged read: out/conf/app.conf' (RULES 16).
  • A match else may start its own line, but an if's } else { may not (RULES 2b).
  • The report needs a separate event because brings commit per event (RULES 12b).
  • A failure is a message, not an exception (RULES 28b).

The saves became identities. Go further: turn every line and word of a document into an identity and ask it questions.

30

A text file becomes identities

Turn a document's lines and words into marked identities, chain phases through events, and query them once they exist.

~5 min · file_words.vein

Open withtarget $Line #Heading is a sentence about a document.

Say
  • The Parser walks lines(f.text), which strips the line ending whichever it was, and captures let number = Index + 1 because the inner loop rebinds Index.
  • Each line becomes an identity: bring Line(number, line, len(words(line))) as e.
  • A blank line gets mark e #Blank, and a line whose first word is exactly # gets mark e #Heading. The decision is made once and remembered as a mark.
  • Inside target words(line) as w, each word is brought as a Word. The mark goes on e, the line from the enclosing loop.
  • emit @Parsed ends the phase. Nothing brought above is committed yet, so the next event is where the identities exist.
  • The report's target $Line #Heading as l prints 'heading at line 1: # VeinScript' and 'heading at line 6: # Why identities', then '40 words; longest is 'identities.''.

One pass over the lines; capture the line number

Lines and words become identities, and marks record decisions

A later phase asks the document a question

Run it
Watch out
  • Running it writes samples/sample-doc.txt and samples/sample-doc.report.txt next to the source file. Delete them after filming.
  • A target $Line in the same handler would match nothing (RULES 11, 12b).
  • Index belongs to the nearest loop (RULES 14c).
  • The comment at lines 141-143 says the language can't inspect characters. That's dated: line[0] and chars() work (RULES 28).
  • The header's lines[i].startsWith("#") is a contrast with method syntax VeinScript doesn't have. String functions are plain functions (RULES 28).

The rules that bite

From docs/RULES.md. The first-hour ones are marked; every one was learned by getting it wrong.

  1. 1
    A newline ends a statement, so a continuation must END the line it continues from (a trailing + or a trailing ,). first hour
    wrong
    right
  2. 2
    There is no != and no ! at all: inequality is not (a == b) and negation is not x (VS0006). Logic is written in words. first hour
    wrong
    right
  3. 2b
    } else { goes on ONE line; an else starting its own line is VS0104 (match arms are exempt). first hour
    wrong
    right
  4. 3
    A string literal is one line; the escapes are \n \t \r \\ \"; a literal newline inside quotes is VS0003. first hour
  5. 4
    Lexer keywords are reserved in expressions but most are still legal as field names. RULES says 63; the lexer has 62 today, so check the map before choosing a name. first hour
    wrong
  6. 5
    A builder's OUTPUT FIELD NAME decides what it makes: markup→@Html, css→@Style, code→@Script, line→@Print, a mark member→identity, inherited→what the base builds, none→@BuilderName. first hour
  7. 6
    So markup, css, code and line cannot be parameter names; doing so reports VS0205 at every call site and nothing at the declaration. first hour
    wrong
  8. 7
    A mark member makes a builder an identity template: bring = spawn + attach each shape + mark. first hour
    right
  9. 7b
    bring X(…) as name binds the identity a template built; as on a fragment builder is VS0221 and it cannot combine with a count (VS0222).
  10. 7c
    A variant (builder BigCoin from Coin { value = 5 }) fixes a base's arguments BY NAME and inherits its marks; a cycle is VS0239 and an unknown base is VS0238.
    right
  11. 8
    A $Shape include is a compile-time field expansion and bring attaches nothing, so a target on that shape matches zero. first hour
    wrong
  12. 9
    Arguments bind positionally across includes in declaration order; ask veinc scaffold <file> '&Name' rather than counting. first hour
    right
  13. 10
    spawn() is the only way to make an entity; with no spawn the world is empty and every target matches nothing. first hour
  14. 11
    spawn is immediate; attach, unattach, mark, unmark and destroy are DEFERRED to the commit point after the folds. first hour
  15. 12
    A structural change is invisible inside the event that made it; seed worlds in run once. first hour
  16. 12b
    …but the NEXT event sees it, because commit is per event; run once commits once for all shards, and wiring and rendering cannot see each other within one @Request.
  17. 12c
    A nested target binds BY NAME, so both the outer and inner bindings are readable in both runtimes.
    right
  18. 13
    folds reconciles concurrent writes (two hp -= 1 give hp - 2); only settled sees the reconciled value, so death checks belong there. first hour
  19. 13b
    folds ACCUMULATES across ticks and does not recompute; a child can write its parent's component through a handle (c.Parent.of.Deck.count += 1).
  20. 13c
    $Parent makes $Position LOCAL and the runtime publishes $World before settled; anything reading world coordinates asks for $World.
  21. 14
    target binds ONE shape set per loop (several shapes is an AND), and nothing can ask an identity which shapes it carries.
  22. 14b
    Query order is spawn order unless by Shape.field sorts it at read time (stable, strings compared ordinally).
    right
  23. 14c
    Index is the nearest loop's 0-based counter; it counts position in yield order and does NOT sort.
    right
  24. 14d
    ordered by &Builder.$Shape.param { bring … } sorts the BRINGS, which is how fragment output (most of a web page) gets ordered.
    right
  25. 14e
    ordered by also takes a target loop, which is how DATA gets ordered; only bring is reordered.
    right
  26. 15
    $Enemy and #Enemy are different things: a different keyword and a different sigil, and a program may use both. first hour
  27. 15b
    Components unify by bare name across bundles, and a shape cannot include a shape (VS0007); a field mismatch is VS0220 or VS0332.
  28. 15c
    A shape may BRING marks, which arrive and leave with it in the same commit.
    right
  29. 16
    A mark is just a name unless declared; a bundle that declares any mark has its mark names checked (VS0218).
    right
  30. 17
    Only shared("…") inside a publicator crosses a bundle boundary; everything else is bundle-private.
  31. 17b
    The qualified *A.B.P.$Shape / #Mark form is for INCLUDES and DISCOVERY; target, mark, audience and match take a bare name.
  32. 17c
    An IMPORTED $Shape becomes a real component once something attaches it; target it by its bare name.
    right
  33. 17d
    The shared("…") string is a LABEL shown in the completion row; over 160 characters is the VS0243 warning.
  34. 18
    need "Author.Bundle" names a dependency, widens bare names (lookup order: local → built-in → need) and LINKS the bundle; use is VS0338, a missing author is VS0339 and an unknown bundle is VS0340. first hour
    wrong
    right
  35. 18b
    need "Author.Bundle" as Y imports QUALIFIED only (*Y.…) and widens nothing; this is the answer to a VS0216 ambiguity.
    right
  36. 19
    A bundle can span files (publicators/.vein for API, shards/.vein for behaviour); fragments merge BEFORE the main file, and an API declaration in a fragment is VS0321.
  37. 20
    An event is Author.Bundle.Name while a shape is just its name; runtime and stdlib events (@Request, @Print, @Ticked) keep bare names.
  38. 20b
    An SF runs INLINE (its brings land where you called it); a shard hearing an event does not.
  39. 21
    bring and emit QUEUE, they do not write; the queue drains only after every handler of the current event has finished.
  40. 22
    veinc serve gives every request a fresh interpreter, so run once re-runs per request; veinc render is the same pipeline, one-shot.
  41. 23
    Under Git Bash, pass MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 for a / argument, or the path becomes C:/Program Files/Git/. first hour
    wrong
    right
  42. 24
    There are four checks guarding different things: dotnet test (behaviour), check-ir.sh (IR shape), check-backend.sh (backend meaning), check-perf.sh (speed).
  43. 24b
    JSON crosses the boundary with fromJson(text) and toJson(shape); integral numbers parse as int, malformed input is null, and both are interpreter-only.
    right
  44. 25
    When measuring the backend, use Release on both sides and measure past JIT warm-up.
  45. 26
    Arity and literal types are checked (VS0204, VS0228, VS0227, VS0229, VS0230); nothing else about a value is, and a missing value reads as empty, not zero. first hour
    wrong
  46. 27
    target rows as row: $Row declares what OUTSIDE data looks like, so fields are checked and read directly (row.title); an unknown shape is VS0233.
    right
  47. 28
    A character is a one-character string: no char type and no 'a' literal; two strings compare ordinally.
    right
  48. 28a
    Splitting is done by the host: split keeps empties, lines strips \r, words drops empties, plus chars and trim; all return lists.
    wrong
    right
  49. 28d
    Conversions are named after the type (int, float, string, bool) and are total (int("abc") is 0); guard with isNumber.
    right
  50. 28e
    Ordering decides in three steps: both text → ordinal; both numeric (parsed text included) → numeric; otherwise ordinal on text, never silently zero.
  51. 28b
    A file is an event and a failure is a message: @ReadFile answers @FileLoaded or @FileMissing, and there is no catch.
    right
  52. 28c
    Route file events by tag, not by path; a tag is a mark checked in when arms, so a typo is caught at compile time as a VS0218 warning (in a bundle that declares its marks).
    right

What VeinScript deliberately doesn't have

idnot herewrite insteadwhy
D1C-style typed parameters such as int v (and mixed hp : int / int v)name: Type everywhere: fn clamp(v: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int, let x: T = …One rule that reads left to right. Leaving out : Type is then naturally just let x = ….
D2when cond { … } as a general conditionalif / else if / else. when is only the arm keyword inside match.Identity comes from shape/shard/target, not from renaming conditionals. when is kept for match arms.
D3for, in, looptarget coll as x { … } for any collection or query, repeat N [as i] { … } for counting, while cond { … }, plus break/continuetarget unifies iterating data with querying identities, which is the central IOP verb. The language reads as targeting sets rather than running C-style loops.
D4push (a field-write keyword)Compound assignment (self.Health.hp -= 1). When several shards write one field, the shape declares a reducer: hp: int folds sum.It separates the per-shard write from the merge policy, which is declared once on the data. The result is deterministic and independent of shard order.
D5classData in shape (component), type (plain value) and event (message). All behaviour in shard.The data/behaviour split is what makes folds, deterministic scheduling and parallelism possible. Web and desktop are modelled as identities + shards too.
D6A function that both emits and returns, or an SF with a return valuefn f(…) -> T { return … } for values; SF f(…) { emit … } for named emit sequences (-> T on an SF is VS0105, return outside an fn is VS0107)'Returns a value' versus 'emits events' can be decided from the declaration alone. Purity cannot be checked, so a 'verified pure' promise could not be kept.
D7SemicolonsA newline ends a statement (a virtual terminator). To continue an expression, end the line with an operator or comma.The lexer's newline terminator (CanEndStatement) was kept, and blocks use braces.
D8The :: scope operator (::Health.hp, M::x)self.Health.hp (name the target binding) and *Author.Bundle.Publicator.member for cross-bundle references:: carried two unrelated meanings, and both already had a better spelling. M::x had zero uses in samples/ and stdlib/.
D9List mutation: append, sort in place, pushBuild lists with [a, b, c] or with split/lines/words/chars. Use len, xs[i], target xs as x, pick, join. Order with ordered by or target … by.Lists exist as values you can build, index, measure and iterate. Mutation has not been designed yet.
D10User-defined genericsBuilt-in collections onlyDeferred and low priority. Built-ins are special-cased in v1.
D11Top-level enum declarationsDeclare the enum inside the shape that owns it: shape $Match { enum State { Kickoff, Play, Over } state: State } (top level is VS0102)State definitions stay next to the data they constrain, with no floating global enum namespace. Meaning attaches to identities.
D12! and !=not x and not (a == b). The parentheses matter: not x == y is (not x) == y, and VS0008 warns about it.and/or/not are already words, so a symbolic exception would be inconsistent. A dropped ! flips a condition and still compiles. This is also the general rule: 'C does it' is not an argument.
D13Descending order and sorting by more than one component fieldtarget $Row #Row by Row.rank as r { … }: ascending, stable, strings compared ordinallySorting at read time keeps entity ids stable, so references to rows are never disturbed. Only ascending order on one field has been built.

Glossary

termsyntaxmeaningfirst seen
Identity Oriented Programming (IOP)shape · mark · event · shard · targetThe paradigm. A program is a set of identities that carry data and tags. All behaviour lives in shards, which target matching identities. There is no class, and shards never call each other.demo.vein
Identity / Entitylet e = spawn() · EntitySomething in the world: an id that shapes and marks hang off. Entity is also a keyword. As a type it is an entity id. As an expression it is the id of the nearest target binding, or 0 outside a target.entities.vein
spawn()let e = spawn()A built-in call, not a keyword. It creates an identity immediately and is the only way to make one. With no spawn the world is empty and every target matches nothing.entities.vein
Shapeshape $Health { hp: int folds sum } · $HealthA named group of fields an identity carries (a component). Across bundles, shapes with the same bare name are the same component. A shape can declare an enum and can bring marks with it.entities.vein
Mark#Enemy · mark e #Enemy · unmark self #Enemy · mark #Enemy (declaration)A tag with no fields that an identity wears. Declaring any mark at bundle level turns on VS0218 checking for that bundle. Used as a value, a mark evaluates to its own name, which is how console addresses and file tags work.entities.vein
Eventevent @Hit { amount: int = 1 }A message type. A field with = is optional and one without is required. Since the last commits, an event's identity is Author.Bundle.Name, while a shape's is just its name.payload.vein
emitemit @Hit { amount: 5 }Queues an event. It does not deliver right away. Omitted fields are filled from defaults, then from context (the event being heard, then locals).payload.vein
hearhear @Hit as h { … h.amount … }A handler block. The binding reads payload fields directly, with no sigil.payload.vein
Provenance envelopes.from.kind · s.from.name · origin · cause · trailFields the runtime attaches to every event: id, from, origin, source, bundle, cause, trail. You never declare them. veinc events prints them.payload.vein
audiencehear @E as e audience $Session #Trusted { … }A barrier on a handler: it fires only when the emitter carries every listed shape and mark. It is enforced over Vein.Net (signed frames) and only advisory over the local console pipe.events.vein
Shardshard Drain { each tick { … } settled { … } }The only place behaviour lives: a set of schedule and hear blocks. A shard can never be shared or put inside a publicator (VS0108).entities.vein
target (identity query)target $Health #Enemy as self { self.Health.hp -= 1 }Loops over every identity that carries ALL the listed shapes and marks. Fields are read as binding.Shape.field. At least one shape is required (VS0236). Results come in spawn order unless a by clause sorts them.entities.vein
target (collection)target words(s) as w { … } · target rows as row: $Task { … }The same verb iterates any list. There is no for/in. An optional : $Shape ascription declares what outside data (JSON, DB rows) looks like, so its fields are checked.loops.vein
run oncerun once { … }A schedule that runs once at start. This is where worlds are seeded. run and once are contextual words, not keywords.entities.vein
each tick / each frameeach tick { … }A schedule that runs every simulation tick. The clock is explicit: veinc run … --ticks N.entities.vein
settledsettled { … }Runs after the tick's fold contributions are reconciled. This is the only correct place to read final values, such as death checks.entities.vein
every Nevery 2 { … }A wall-clock timer, in seconds.console_broadcast.vein
foldshp: int folds sumA field modifier that says how writes from several shards in one tick combine: sum, min, max, replace, first, all, any. It accumulates across ticks and does not recompute.entities.vein
attach / unattachattach $Health to e { hp: 5 } · unattach $Health from eAdds or removes a component. The change is deferred to the commit point, so it is invisible inside the event that made it and visible from the next one.entities_detach.vein
destroydestroy selfRemoves an identity. The removal is deferred like the other structural changes.entities_destroy.vein
IndexIndexThe nearest loop's 0-based iteration counter, in target and repeat. Where Entity says which identity, Index says which iteration. It does not sort anything.entities_index.vein
SF (shard function)SF announce(label: string, value: int) { emit @E { … } }A named sequence of emits that runs inline. It never returns: -> T is VS0105 and return is VS0107.functions.vein
fnfn fib(n: int) -> int { … return … }A function that computes and returns a value. It can be called in any expression, and across bundles when shared.functions.vein
builderbuilder Button { label: string markup = "<button>" + label + "</button>" }A reusable template. Its members are its parameters, with no ( ) parameter list. Its output field decides what it makes. A builder cannot hold statements.mypage.vein
bringbring Button("+1") · bring 3 Card(…)Instantiates a builder, binding arguments by position. The fragment it produces is queued, not written. A leading count repeats it.mypage.vein
Output-channel fieldmarkup = … · css = … · code = … · line = …The field NAME picks the channel: @Html, @Style, @Script, @Print. With no such field the builder emits @BuilderName. For this reason these four words cannot be parameter names.mypage.vein
$Shape includebuilder Card { $Card markup = … }A compile-time copy of a shape's fields into a builder's or event's parameters. It attaches nothing: target $Card still matches zero identities.shaped.vein
Identity templatebuilder Unit { $Health $Shield mark #Unit } · bring Unit(10, 6) as uA builder with a mark member builds an identity: bring = spawn + attach each shape + mark. as binds the identity it built.entities_template.vein
Builder variantbuilder BigCoin from Coin { value = 5 }Fixes some of a base builder's arguments BY NAME and inherits its marks. A fixed parameter takes no argument. A cycle is VS0239.builder_variants.vein
? fill-the-rest / basebring Draft("Untitled", ?) · bring Panel("Danger", base, …)? fills every remaining slot with its default, or a typed zero when there is none. base fills one slot with its declared default without skipping it.builder_defaults.vein
ShardViewShardView Page { hear @Html as h { … } }A First-Class object that ASSEMBLES. It hears fragments and emits the finished artifact, such as the @Response page.site.vein
bridgebridge Sync { hear @Hit as h { emit @SyncedHit } }A shard-like First-Class object that spans a boundary. It shows up as Bridge.Sync in veinc graph and in provenance.payload.vein
Bundlebundle Functions by you { … }The module. by author roots its qualified name. It is private by default and can span files (publicators/.vein is API, shards/.vein is behaviour).functions.vein
publicator + sharedpublicator DemoCore { shared("…") shape $Health { … } }A publicator is a bundle's API grouping. Only shared("label") members can be used from another bundle. The label is shown in completion, and over 160 characters is VS0243.demo.vein
needneed "Vein.Console" · need "Vein.Math" as MNames the bundle this one is built on. It lets bare names resolve (lookup order: local → built-in → need) and links the bundle into an app. With as, names are imported qualified only (*M.…). use is retired (VS0338).entities.vein
Qualified star path*Vein.Console.Io.@Print · *Vein.Math.Scalars.clamp(…)A reference that cannot collide: *Author.Bundle.Publicator.member. It is used for includes, cross-bundle emits, calls and discovery. target and mark take bare names.entities.vein
app / load / principalapp Shop { load "Store.vein" load "Billing.vein" }A manifest listing bundles. The first load is the principal and the only one that boots. Every loaded bundle's shards join ONE runtime.samples/app_capabilities/shop.app.vein
startstart @NewGame { seed: 42, players: 2 }A bundle's boot event, at most one per bundle. It replaces the default @Request { path }. It can be overridden with --set k=v or load … start { … }.boot.vein
chancechance 30% { … }A block that runs with a given probability. 30% is a single token. It lowers to random() < 0.30 using a seeded generator, so runs are reproducible.entities_chance.vein
match / whenmatch m.Match.state { when Kickoff { … } else { … } }Branches by NAME, on an enum case or a #Mark. Arms cannot be string literals, so routing on a web path uses if.match_orders.vein
enum (inside a shape)shape $Match { enum State { Kickoff, Play, Over } state: State }The states a field can hold. An enum can only be declared inside a shape (top level is VS0102). A case evaluates to its own name.enum_state.vein
Loopsrepeat 3 as r { … } · while i < 10 { … } · break · continueCounted and conditional loops alongside target. There is no for/in/loop.loops.vein
Orderingtarget $Row #Row by Row.rank as r { … } · ordered by &Card.rank { bring … }by Shape.field sorts a query when it is read (stable, strings compared ordinally). ordered by sorts brings, which is how fragments and data rows get ordered.entities_ordered.vein
here() / console rolesmatch here() { when #Main { … } when #Alpha { … } }This process's own console address. One program acts out several roles across windows.console_roles.vein
$Parent / $Worldattach $Parent to crate { of: platform } · t.World.xA parented $Position is local. The runtime composes the chain and publishes $World, which holds absolute coordinates.transform_hierarchy.vein

The toolchain

commandwhat it does
veinc new <bundle|app> <Name> [--author A] [-o <parentDir>]Scaffolds a new bundle or app project on disk. It writes files, so don't run it inside the repo.
veinc check <file.vein>Runs the full front end, including Lower where most VS02xx codes are raised, and prints only diagnostics. It prints 'ok' when the file is clean and exits 1 on errors.
veinc tokens <file.vein>Lexer output: span, TokenKind and text for each token. It shows sigil folding, 30% as one Percent token, and the virtual Term at a newline.
veinc ast <file.vein>Prints the parsed AST.
veinc ir <file.vein> [--ir-unicode] [--ir-spans] [--ir-full-strings] [--ir=legacy]The VeinIR ASCII tree, which is what check-ir.sh compares against golden files. It also reports Lower diagnostics.
veinc run <file|app.vein> [--ticks N]A console session: boots the program, pumps stdin/stdout through @Input/@Print, advances N ECS ticks, and runs every N timers and the network. An app manifest is linked into one runtime first.
veinc render <file> [path] [--set k=v] [--ticks N]One shot: fires the boot event or @Request { path } and prints the emit trace, the HTTP status and the @Response body. No socket is involved.
veinc serve <file> --port N [--host H]A real HTTP server over the same @Request → @Response pipeline, with a fresh interpreter for every request.
veinc build <file> [--rid R] [--framework-dependent]Builds a standalone .exe that embeds the interpreter and the source, via dotnet publish. --rid linux-x64 cross-builds for a VPS. It writes an exe.
veinc emit <file|app> -o <dir>Translates HIR to readable C# for the SECS backend, covering the identity half: shapes, marks, target, folds, run once/each tick/settled. It reports interpreter-only built-ins such as fromJson and split.
veinc graph <file> [path]The First-Class graph from one render: nodes (Shard/Bridge/ShardView/Runtime) and emit edges, e.g. Bridge.Sync --@local.Demo.SyncedHit-->.
veinc events <file> [--json]Lists every event with each field marked required or default, plus the provenance envelope.
veinc scaffold <file> <@Event | &Builder | Name>Prints a ready-to-paste emit body or bring call. Every slot is labelled with its type, the shape it came from, and whether it is required or optional.
veinc symbols <app.vein> [--json]Discovery across bundles: every shared member as *Author.Bundle.Publicator.member, with collisions flagged and start signatures shown.
veinc exec <file> [--json] [--ascii]The derived execution model, from static analysis: block classes ◆◉◷▣∞, parallel ⚡ / synchronized 🔒 / conflict !, and waves.
.\veinc.cmd <cmd> · dotnet run --project src/Vein.Cli -- <cmd>Two ways to invoke the CLI from the repo (a wrapper script or dotnet run).
dotnet build VeinScript.slnBuilds the compiler, CLI, Workbench, tests and SECS runtime.
dotnet test src/Vein.TestsBehaviour tests, including SamplesTests: every sample compiles with zero warnings and every header command is runnable.
bash tools/check-ir.shCompares printed IR trees against golden files (the IR's shape).
bash tools/check-backend.shCompiles the listed samples to C#, runs them, and diffs their output against the interpreter byte for byte (the backend's meaning).
bash tools/check-perf.shMeasures backend speed. Release build, past JIT warm-up.
dotnet test src/Vein.Jit.TestsThe net9 JIT test suite, kept separate because Vein.Tests is net8.
dotnet run --project src/Vein.WorkbenchLaunches the Workbench desktop IDE (Avalonia).
bash tools/ship.shProduces out/standalone/ and the per-user installer out/installer/VeinScript-Workbench-win-Setup.exe (Velopack).

The Workbench

VeinScript Workbench: a desktop IDE (Avalonia). Start it with dotnet run --project src/Vein.Workbench or install it with VeinScript-Workbench-win-Setup.exe, which installs per user under %LOCALAPPDATA% so the samples stay editable. The first launch opens on the samples, and Help ▸ Browse Samples gets back to them later.

Worth showing on camera:

  • ▶ runs what the file declares. The file's header line (// veinc run samples/entities_chance.vein --ticks 4) becomes an editable command box in the toolbar, so you can change --ticks 4 to --ticks 40 and press ▶. Each session shows its exit code and duration (exited 2 · 1.4s) and has ↻ to re-run and ⤓ to save the full log.
  • Compile as you type. About 450 ms after you stop typing, red underlines appear and the Diagnostics list (filterable by severity and text) refreshes. Quick fixes exist only where the fix is mechanically certain: VS0228 inserts ?, VS0218 declares the mark, and VS0338/VS0339 rewrite use Movement into need "kit.Movement".
  • Sigil completion: $ shapes, # marks, @ events, & builders, * qualified names, . members. Typing ? right after emit @E or bring B expands into the full field list, with each field's type and the $Shape it came from. A signature-help strip marks the current slot in a bring.
  • Navigation across bundles: F12 (it works on a need line too), Shift+F12 to find references, Ctrl+T to search symbols, Ctrl+Shift+F to find in files, the Outline pane, and Alt+←/→ to go back and forward.
  • Runtime panel: the killer demo. A tick stepper, an event timeline and an entity browser. Boot the world, step one tick at a time, and watch identities and their components change. This replaces a line debugger, because shards never call each other.
  • Execution tab (the veinc exec model): each block gets a badge (◆ Event, ◉ Reactive, ◷ Scheduled, ▣ Frame, ∞ Continuous) plus ⚡ parallel / 🔒 synchronized / ! conflict, laid out in waves. It shows that folds sum is what makes two shards safe to run in parallel.
  • Events tab: who emits and who hears each event, with a jump from every row. It flags events that are emitted but never heard, and heard but never emitted.
  • IR Tree / Raw IR: double-click a node to land on the source line that produced it.
  • Terminal: several concurrent sessions, each with its own stdin. Run All Participants (Ctrl+F5) starts control_center.vein's Control → Alpha → Beta in header order. The Consoles topology shows who addresses whom and flags unresolved sends in red. Live shows the bound pipes, and Transcript interleaves all sessions with timestamps.
  • Preview for websites: a route picker built from the site's own if r.path == "…" conditions, the rendered markup with status and headers, Open in Browser, one-click serve, and live reload.
  • Project Explorer for an app.vein: ★ marks the principal and 📦 its dependencies. The Bundle Inspector shows a PUBLIC/SHARED/PRIVATE bar. The Symbols tab lists every primitive under the author and bundle that brought it, with collisions highlighted.
  • Build ▸ Publish Executable (runs veinc build), Run Checks (check-ir.sh, check-backend.sh, …) from a menu, and New Project templates for a CLI app, chat app or website.
  • The UI also has an Assistant panel (sign-in; every suggestion is compiled before an Insert button is offered) and a Lounge panel (a shared chat room). They are not described in docs/WORKBENCH.md, so check both live before putting them in the video.
  • Not there: an embedded web view (C1b, deliberately left out; Open in Browser covers it).

Reserved, not implemented

  • mute: lexed only, with no parser reference. mute A in a tick block → VS0104 "Unexpected 'mute' in expression".
  • unmute: lexed only. unmute A → VS0104.
  • transform: lexed only. At bundle level → VS0102 "Unexpected 'transform' at declaration level".
  • on: lexed only. on click { } in a shard → VS0103 "Unexpected 'on' in shard body". It is still legal as a field name (samples/sigil_names.vein shape $Switch { on: int }).
  • sync: lexed, and CanEndStatement knows it, but no parser case. shard A sync { → VS0100, in a shard body → VS0103, in a tick block → VS0104, even though LANGUAGE.md/KEYWORDS.md describe it.
  • count: lexed only. let n = count $H → VS0104. It is still fine as a field name (entities_tree count: int folds sum), and the size of a list is len(x).
  • map: lexed, but map<string,int> in type position → VS0100 "Expected type, found KwMap".
  • use: lexed and parsed only so it can be rejected. Every use is VS0338 telling you to write need "Author.Bundle" (retired rather than unbuilt).
  • NOT unimplemented, despite what the docs say: enum works inside a shape (samples/enum_state.vein runs; only top-level is VS0102, by design D11); random is no longer a keyword and random() works; bridge, audience, builder, bring, base, ShardView, Index, need and app are all implemented.

Every sample

Full source, coloured like the editor. Use the filter at the top to find every sample that uses a keyword or a concept.

Core language 14

samples/demo.veinDemo: the IOP core in one filegood

A compact tour of the core syntax: a shared $Health shape whose hp folds by sum, an @Damaged event, an SF, and a Drain shard that drains every #Enemy each tick, emits damage by chance, and marks the dead in settled. It never spawns anything, so it compiles and runs but prints nothing.

Teaches
bundle / publicator / shared shape with a folds sum field event with an included $Shape field and a var member SF (shard function that emits) shard schedules: each tick and settled target query over shape + mark chance N% mark (deferred structural change) sigils $ # @
Needs first
what an entity/identity is the idea of a per-frame tick
Level
●●○○○ · 62 lines

No run command in the header. veinc run samples/demo.vein --ticks 3 exits 0 with no output (empty world). The output field holds an excerpt of veinc ir samples/demo.vein (the Shard Drain subtree), which matches the on-screen excerpt; the full IR is 33 lines. SF hurt is declared but never called (the header says so on purpose). docs/EXAMPLE-PIPELINE.md traces this file's emit through AST, HIR, IR and the backend.

samples/payload.veinEvent payloads: defaults and auto-fillgood

Shows three ways a payload gets its values: a field default (@Hit amount = 1), auto-fill of an omitted field from the event being heard (a bridge re-emits @SyncedHit with no body), and plain dot access on the hear binding. The response reports where the event came from via the auto-tagged from origin.

Teaches
event field defaults emit with omitted fields (default or auto-fill from context) hear ... as binding and plain field access bridge as a First-Class object event origin tagging (from.kind / from.name) render pipeline: @Request in, @Response out
Needs first

Level
●●○○○ · 27 lines

The · trace lines go to stderr; HTTP 200 and the body go to stdout. The run used MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1. The file is in tools/check-backend.sh (payload.vein:2).

samples/events.veinAudience: who may be heardcore

Two shards emit @Damage on the same request: Combat carries $Session #Trusted and Sneaky carries nothing. The Auditor's hear ... audience $Session #Trusted lets Combat's event through and blocks Sneaky's, and the render trace logs the block.

Defines the two kinds of function, a value-returning fn (bonus, recursive fib) and an event-emitting SF (announce), then calls them locally and calls shared ones from other bundles through the qualified *Vein.Math / *Vein.Console paths.

samples/loops.veinFour loops, break and continuecore

Runs VeinScript's four loops (while, repeat N as i, target over a list, target over identities) and cuts them short with break and continue: while uses both, a capped repeat uses break, and both target loops use continue. Players are brought in run once and reported in a separate each-tick schedule.

Seeds four orders with string statuses, then three independent shards each run their own target loop over the same orders with a different match. An Odometer identity is advanced by hearing the stdlib clock event *Vein.Time.Clock.@Ticked rather than by each tick. It records the event's frame number and accumulates the runtime's fixed delta, and a settled shard prints the elapsed time rounded with Vein.Math.

samples/diagnostics.veinNo try/catch: failure is a messagecore

Shows what VeinScript has instead of try/catch: a Collector shard hears @DiagnosticRaised from anywhere in the program. Some diagnostics are raised on purpose with info/warn/error SFs, and one comes from a real runtime fault (5 % 0) that stops only its own block while the other shards carry on.

Teaches
@DiagnosticRaised as the catch severity levels 0/1/2 *Vein.Diagnostics.Report.info/warn/error SFs runtime faults become events; the block stops, the program lives event queue ordering failure events like @Failed / @Undelivered
Needs first

Level
●●●○○ · 127 lines · in lesson 7

The header's 'Delete shard Collector below and the same six lines still appear' has the wrong count. With the Collector deleted (tested on a copy), FOUR diagnostics still print in the runtime's own format: (info: 2 rows to check), (warning: a row has an empty title), (error: a row has rank -1, which is not a rank) and (error: Compute (once): Attempted to divide by zero.). They print inline, right after the line that raised them, instead of after the plain prints. The live edit works, but say 'four lines' and expect the order to change. The Unreachable shard hears *Vein.Net.Http.@Failed, which never fires here (no HTTP request), so it only illustrates the pattern. The row with an empty title and rank -1 is still brought and printed, because Validate reports but does not reject.

samples/diagnostics_guard.veinGuards: checking what arrivedgood

Rows arrive as @RowArrived events, including one built from JSON with a misspelt key, and a Guard shard on that boundary rejects rows with no title (error), keeps suspicious ranks with a warning, and reports a total (info). It demonstrates that a static check catches what you wrote while a guard catches what arrived.

Teaches
guard shard on a boundary event choosing error vs warn vs info missing values read as empty, not zero fromJson and runtime-only field names target ... by Shape.field ordering if / } else { on one line multi-line concatenation with trailing +
Needs first

Level
●●●●○ · 137 lines

Interpreter-only because of fromJson, and not in check-backend. The output shows '4 rows arrived' while only three rows are kept, because the empty-title row was rejected. The ordering of kept rows comes from by Row.rank, where the empty rank sorts first.

●●○○○ · 62 lines

BROKEN OUTPUT, fix before filming. The page renders an empty <style>, <body> and <script>, even though the trace shows 11 @Html, 1 @Style and 1 @Script emitted. Cause: fragment builders emit the bare stdlib channel name (src/Vein.Compiler/Ir/Lower.cs:2123 hardcodes "Html"/"Script"/"Style"). Since commit 0b4ce31 ("An event is Author.Bundle.Name"), this bundle's own event @Html/@Script/@Style declarations are keyed @local.App.*. The ShardView's hear @Html resolves to that local event, so no builder fragment reaches it. Kernel's explicit emit @Render does resolve locally (trace: @local.App.Render), which is why a 200 still comes back. Fix, tested on a scratch copy: delete the three lines event @Html, event @Script and event @Style from PageApi (deleting the whole PageApi publicator also works). The view then hears Vein.Web's events, which the file already needs. The page comes back with the stylesheet, the heading, the counter, the button, eight <li>row</li> items and the inc() script. Once fixed, this would be a core sample.

samples/db_supabase.veinSupabase read and writegood

Holds Supabase credentials as a $Connection identity, GETs a tasks table, and turns each returned row into a $Task identity. It then lists the tasks by rank and POSTs a new $Draft row serialised with toJson. All of it is @Fetch/@Fetched events; there's no database driver.

Teaches
credentials as an identity (&Connection) versus an announcement event (&Connect) fromJson list plus ascription target rows as row: $Task emit a follow-up event (@Loaded) because brings are not yet committed an event that includes a stdlib shape (*Vein.Rest.Db.$Connection) a separate $Draft shape for rows without a server-assigned id toJson(d.Draft) for a POST body; Status.ok / clientError
Needs first
identity templates and target queries fromJson/toJson and ascription (json_roundtrip.vein) deferred commit per event (RULES 12b) REST GET/POST basics
